task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-10-06, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
A defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 120 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: defensive suppression of opponent H2-H1 change
half-to-half scoring change (H2-H1) as a team trait
team-level defensive effect stability across seasons
regression to the mean in second-half versus first-half scoring
counter strategy best and avoid defensive schemes
methodological_questions: Is a team's defensive effect on opponents' H2-H1 change stable across split halves of the same season or across adjacent seasons, after removing regression to the mean?
What reliability and between-team variance can 120 team-seasons detect, and what confidence interval does the estimate carry?
How should opponent quality, pace, score state, starters and rotation be adjusted when estimating a defense's effect on half-to-half change?
Is the H2-H1 defensive effect distinguishable from a permutation null built by shuffling team labels within season?

historical_evidence.finding: H1 play-type usage as a predictor of H2 suppression (n=8873 team-games; Test C n=1008). Matched ATT for PNR was +0.0313 with BH_p=0.0658 (WEAK); the other BH-adjusted tests were null. Top-1 accuracy was 0.550 against a mean-reversion baseline of 0.511 (+0.039). [prior work] states that the bulk of H2 suppression is regression to the mean.

Adapter-based defensive adjustment test (T1 dPPP: adapter +0.0667 n=205, neutral +0.0248 n=50, no_signal +0.1260 n=57, wrong_way +0.0111 n=274). Its T2 adapter-minus-no-signal gaps were negative (-0.0361 at 1 vote, -0.1170 at 2 votes). Its next-game PPP test was null (Welch t=-1.003, p=0.842). [prior work] classifies the apparent effect as a construction, selection or labelling artifact.

Defensive scheme change within and across games using inferred labels: within-game change 319/523 (61.0%), cross-game change 298/440 (67.7%), transition matrices near-uniform. [prior work]'s caveat is that the inferred label cannot separate real defensive adjustment from offense executing differently.

Play-type PPP change across playoff series game buckets (1197 pooled records, min 10 possessions, min 3 series, no CIs). DRIVE 0.889 to 0.949 (+0.060); CUT +0.114; PNR +0.087; PULL_UP -0.077; POST_UP -0.032. [prior work] states 'NO CLEAR SIGNAL' and flags selection caveats.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Predicting second-half suppression from first-half play-type reliance, with and without matched controls and BH correction
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as an adequately powered null (B_powered_null). Matched ATT did not survive BH correction, and predictive lift over the mean-reversion baseline was only +0.039. Regression to the mean accounts for most of the H2 suppression.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using an inferred scheme-vote label to detect a defensive adaptation effect on PPP and its carryover to the next game
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as an artifact (C_artifact) with label-error and selection/regression-to-the-mean limitations. The next-game carryover test was null and the confidence gradient reversed sign.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Measuring defensive scheme change from inferred labels
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as unanswerable (A_unanswerable). Transition matrices were near-uniform, which [prior work] describes as consistent with label noise, and the labels cannot separate defense from offense.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Detecting a series-progression pattern in play-type PPP using pooled game buckets
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as unclear (E_unclear) with no clear signal, no confidence intervals, and selection caveats.

evidence_establishes: In earlier project work, the observed second-half suppression of opponents was largely explained by regression to the mean rather than by a stable, predictive team-level defensive signal ([prior work][prior work]).
Inferred defensive-label constructs in this project were fragile and were recorded as artifacts or unanswerable ([prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work]).
Half-to-half and series-progression PPP signals in earlier project work were small, unconfirmed or unclear once selection was considered ([prior work][prior work]).
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests whether a team's defensive effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is reliable across split halves or seasons. None reports a team-season reliability coefficient.
No retrieved record uses the 120 team-season unit or the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data described in the task.
The retrieved records concern play-type PPP, usage and inferred scheme labels, not the H2-H1 scoring-change outcome itself. Their results cannot be transferred directly to it.
Nothing here shows whether the outcome is reliable at 120 team-seasons, or what power such a sample gives.
own_inferences: The H2-H1 outcome is a difference between two noisy half-game scoring rates, so its team-level variance is likely dominated by sampling noise and regression to the mean. The earlier RTM finding makes a reliable trait more doubtful, not less.
With 30 teams per season, adjacent-season correlations rest on about 30 pairs each, so only moderate-to-large reliabilities (roughly r of 0.4 or more) are detectable with reasonable power.
A defensive effect estimated from opponents' H2-H1 change may partly reflect opponent pace, score state and garbage time, which are confounders the retrieved records do not address for this outcome.
uncertainties: Whether the available per-game files support a half-level H2-H1 outcome at the team-game level, and how many possessions each half contains.
The exact definition of the defense effect (for example a mixed-model random effect or a raw opponent-minus-baseline mean) and how it is shrunk.
Whether the 2025-26 playoffs and regular season are included, and whether partial 2025-26 data was used before the complete-data dates.
No follow-up tool was called, so no further record on H2-H1, defensive reliability or power was checked.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records, especially [prior work][prior work] (rejected, RTM-dominated), show that naive H2-H1 suppression signals mostly reflect regression to the mean. Along with the artifact and untestable records on inferred labels, they lower confidence in a direct test. The decision therefore moves from a plain proceed to proceed_with_changes: the study must be a reliability estimate with explicit RTM and permutation nulls, not a claim of a defensive trait. It is not do_not_proceed, because no retrieved record tests the reliability question itself.

blocking_constraints.text: Second-half suppression is largely regression to the mean ([prior work][prior work]). Team effects must be estimated with split-half or cross-season designs and shrunk, or the signal will be mostly noise.
120 team-seasons (about 30 per season) give only about 30 adjacent-season pairs per comparison; only moderate-to-large reliabilities are reliably detectable.
H2-H1 differences built from half-game scoring are noisy; reliability must be estimated before any trait claim.
Opponent quality, pace, score state, garbage time and starter or rotation changes can produce apparent defensive effects on half-to-half change.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests the team-level reliability of a defensive effect on opponents' H2-H1 change. The closest records (SF-[prior work], rejected) find that second-half suppression is mostly regression to the mean. Records on inferred labels (SF-[prior work] artifact, SF-[prior work] untestable) and on series PPP (SF-[prior work] inconclusive) are related but not the same question. Prior work partly answers the question by showing that the naive signal is mostly RTM.

risks.text: Regression to the mean is the main threat, as recorded in [prior work][prior work] and [prior work][prior work]. Selecting teams on a high or low H2-H1 value will inflate apparent stability.
With 120 team-seasons the test has limited power for moderate reliabilities; a null may simply be underpowered.
The H2-H1 outcome and any defense-effect estimate may have low split-half reliability, which can hide a real trait or create a spurious one.
Any scheme or defense label derived from play-by-play may be mislabelled, as recorded in [prior work][prior work] and [prior work][prior work].
Opponent quality, pace, score state, garbage time and rotation can confound the defensive effect on half-to-half change.
Many outcome and defense definitions could be tried; without pre-specification, one could be selected as a trait.
Scoring floors and bounded possession counts can compress the H2-H1 distribution and bias reliability estimates.
Rule and pace changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 can make adjacent-season defensive effects non-comparable.

design.estimand: Between-team variance in the defensive effect on opponents' H2-H1 scoring change, expressed as split-half reliability (Spearman-Brown adjusted) and adjacent-season correlation of shrunken team effects, with 95% CIs. The question is whether this variance exceeds the permutation-null variance.
design.unit: Team-season defensive effect (defense of team T in season S), computed from opponent team-games. The H2-H1 change is computed per opponent game from the per-game play-by-play.
design.sample: 30 teams x 4 seasons (2022-23 to 2025-26) = 120 team-seasons, using regular-season data only as the primary sample, with complete 2025-26 regular season (from 2026-04-13). Playoffs are a separate pre-specified secondary sample. Freeze the data at the retrieval date.
design.power: Pre-specify a minimum detectable reliability, for example r at or above 0.4 with 80% power on about 30 adjacent-season pairs per season pair. Report the achieved CI width. A null CI that excludes the minimum detectable reliability is evidence of absence; a CI that includes it is inconclusive.
design.controls: Estimate the defensive effect with a mixed model that adjusts for opponent offensive quality, pace, score margin at half, garbage-time filter, starters and rotation minutes, and the team's own H1 scoring. Shrink team effects with empirical Bayes. Use the regression-to-the-mean baseline from SF-[prior work] as the benchmark, not the raw H2-H1 difference.
design.falsification: (1) Shuffle team labels within season to form a permutation null for reliability and compare. (2) Run the same pipeline on the offensive H2-H1 change of the same team, as a placebo. (3) Run the pipeline on a pre-game-quality placebo (first-half to first-half within-half splits) to check for artifact. Any result that matches the permutation null or the placebo is not a trait.
design.multiplicity: One primary estimand (split-half reliability of the shrunken defensive effect, regular season). Secondary estimands (adjacent-season correlation, playoffs, offense placebo) are reported with Holm or BH correction across the secondary family and labelled exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Support a reliable team trait only if the primary split-half reliability is at or above the pre-specified minimum (for example 0.4) with a 95% CI excluding the permutation-null 95th percentile, and the adjacent-season correlation is positive with a CI excluding zero, and the result survives the placebo and label-shuffle checks. Reject if the CI excludes the minimum detectable reliability on the upper side. Otherwise report as uncertain.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files (play-by-play, substitution intervals, starters, matchup minutes, box score) for 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons, with 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13 and playoffs complete from 2026-06-21, frozen at the 2026-10-06 retrieval date. Derived play-type graph records are used only as cross-checks, not as the primary outcome.
